quotes.text: Migrations fail because leadership frames them as an IT project. Move the servers, hit the date, don't disrupt the business.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the root cause the episode argues against.

quotes.text: Azure doesn't magically make a broken operating model behave. It amplifies it. In the same way a faster conveyor belt doesn't fix a messy factory floor. It spreads the mess faster.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable analogy for why migration is an operating model change.

quotes.text: Establish the landing zone, identity, policy, network, logging and subscription boundaries before you migrate anything that matters. Because the first workload sets the precedent, the precedent becomes the pattern.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete sequencing rule: platform before workloads.

quotes.text: if your cloud hierarchy mirrors your org chart you've built fragility into governance management groups are not a reporting structure they are policy inheritance surfaces
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear design principle for management group hierarchies.

quotes.text: Modernization is a lagging indicator of platform maturity. If you force it early, you don't modernize faster. You just fail in more expensive ways.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns against refactoring before the platform is stable.

chapters.title: Migration as an IT project: the foundational mistake
Azure is the control plane, not the destination
Landing zones as an organizational contract
Management groups, shared services and hub-and-spoke
Organizational reality: platform teams, CCOE and FinOps
Closing synthesis: the enterprise migration mindset

takeaways: Enterprise Azure migrations fail systemically, not technically: treat them as an operating model change and build the landing zone contract for identity, policy, network and logging before the first workload moves.

Use an environment-first management group hierarchy, shared services subscriptions and hub-and-spoke networking, and treat prioritization as portfolio management across rehost, replatform, refactor and retire.
Run a migration factory with repeatable validation gates, earn modernization through platform maturity, and turn the CCOE into a platform product team that offers paved roads instead of approvals.
hook: Most Azure migrations hit their cutover dates and still leave the business harder to run, with identity drift, broken audit trails and rising costs. This episode is for CIOs, platform teams and architects in regulated enterprises planning a large migration. You learn how to sequence platform, migration factory and modernization so governance holds while workloads move.
